title: 2025 Hedera Africa Hackathon Announces Winners, Becomes the Largest Web3 Hackathon Globally
partialText: The 2025 Hedera Africa Hackathon became the world’s largest Web3 hackathon, with 13,000+ developers and $1M in prizes. Winning projects focused on real-world infrastructure like payments, energy certification, and healthcare. The Hashgraph Association also launched a new Investment Committee to back top builders with multi-million-dollar funding and confirmed a 2026 edition.

title: The Real Cost of Running Small Language Models (SLMs) on Edge Devices
partialText: This article explores the practical limitations of running small language models (SLMs) on local hardware in 2026. It argues that memory bandwidth—not NPUs—is the primary bottleneck, with additional constraints from thermal throttling and limited RAM. The key takeaway is that while edge AI can be cost-effective and viable for certain workloads, achieving enterprise-grade performance requires specialized hardware beyond consumer devices.

title: Rethinking Work, Education, and Income in the AI Era
partialText: This article argues that AI is already reshaping the global economy, accelerating job displacement across creative, logistical, and intellectual sectors. It highlights how traditional education and career paths are failing to keep pace with rapid technological change, creating a widening divide between those who adapt and those who fall behind. The key takeaway is that continuous learning and proactive adaptation are now essential for economic survival.

title: MEXC Ranks No. 2 Globally by Spot Market Share, TokenInsight Reports
partialText: TokenInsight’s Q1 2026 report ranks MEXC as the world’s No. 2 crypto exchange by spot market share at 7.88%. Despite a broader market downturn, MEXC recorded the highest growth among major exchanges, increasing its share by 5.35 percentage points. Its zero-fee model, deep liquidity, and rapid token listings continue to drive user adoption and trading activity globally.

title: The Debug Diaries: How PlayerZero Solved Why Won't These Images Load?
partialText: A human engineer reported broken integration icons. PlayerZero’s AI agent found 14 related issues across OAuth, SSO, CSP, and fonts in 23 minutes—solving problems that would have taken humans ~16 hours across 4 months. The AI proactively traced patterns, fixed root causes, and documented everything, preventing customer-facing issues and improving reliability.

title: The Classic Computer Vision Trick Behind Smooth Image Blending
partialText: This post explains Laplacian Pyramid Blending, a classic computer vision technique that blends images by separating fine details from broad color strokes. By using Gaussian Pyramids to blur and Laplacian Pyramids to isolate edges, you can create buttery-smooth transitions.

title: 7 Essential IP Geolocation API Features Every Developer Needs
partialText: Modern IP geolocation APIs are critical infrastructure, powering fraud prevention, personalization, and routing decisions. The best solutions go beyond location data, offering high accuracy, real-time updates, ASN intelligence, privacy detection, and confidence scoring. Performance, scalability, and developer experience ensure reliable integration, making geolocation a trusted signal across applications.

title: What I Learned Running Both SQL Server and PostgreSQL at Scale
partialText: SQL Server may fail over slightly faster, but PostgreSQL with Patroni offers a strong, production-grade HA stack at a much lower licensing cost.

title: AI Brand Visibility Might Be Measured Wrong. Here's What 6 Months of Data Suggest.
partialText: AI visibility tools measure mention rate - a binary metric that treats position #2 and position #9 the same. After 6 months of running forced ranking with reasoning across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, and Grok, the most actionable signal turned out to be "deal breakers" - specific phrases models repeatedly use to rank brands lower. These phrases are stable, traceable to specific sources, and fixable. The gap between "you were mentioned in 47% of responses" and "you're at position #8 because of this phrase from this source" is the gap between analytics and action.

title: A Long Story About How I Dug Into the PostgreSQL Source Code to Write my Own WAL Receiver
partialText: A developer’s curiosity about pg_receivewal turns into building a PostgreSQL WAL receiver, backup system, and deeper respect for C and database internals.

title: Git Was for Code. AI-Native Systems Need a Proof Layer.
partialText: AI is no longer just assisting software teams, it is participating in the engineering lifecycle itself. That creates a new architectural gap: we can ship faster, but we still struggle to prove what happened, why it happened, who approved it, and what outcome it produced. This article argues that AI-native systems need a proof layer, an evidence architecture that links intent, authority, delivery, and outcomes into something traceable, verifiable, and governable.

title: Digital Marketer Then vs Now: From Campaign Planner to AI Prompt Operator
partialText: AI hasn’t ended marketing, but it has changed the job. Here’s why marketers now act as strategists, editors, filters, and prompt operators.

title: Iran Maps Hormuz Cables as Hybrid Warfare Threat
partialText: The IRGC just mapped seven critical undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz. With 30% of Gulf internet traffic at stake and clear precedents for sabotage, Iran has officially weaponized the digital chokepoint.

title: Rocketry Helps Bitcoin Whether It Likes it Or Not
partialText:

And more.

title: AI Product Management vs Not Traditional Product Management
partialText: AI product management is not traditional PM with a model attached. It requires outcome-first thinking, eval-driven development, feedback loops, trust design, and a systems mindset.

title: AI Tools Read Your Code But Not Your Mind. I Built a Fix.
partialText: AI coding tools understand your syntax but not your intent. contextify-ai is an npm package that hooks into git commit, analyzes your code via AST parsing, asks what you changed and why, and generates a .context.md file next to your component. Top half is prose for humans. Bottom half is YAML for AI tools. A smart-diff skips cosmetic changes so you're not burning API calls on formatting fixes. Works with Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, GitHub Models, and Ollama.
